:::{#exr-ppv-bayes}
#### PPV from Bayes' theorem

Write the [positive predictive value](#def-ppv) of a diagnostic test
in terms of its
[sensitivity](#def-sensitivity),
[specificity](#def-specificity),
and the [prevalence](#def-prevalence) of the disease.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-ppv-bayes}

Abbreviate the sensitivity as $\text{sens}$,
the specificity as $\text{spec}$,
and the prevalence as $\text{prev}$.
By
[Bayes' theorem](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#thm-bayes),
with the probability of a positive test from @exr-prob-positive:

$$
\ba
\text{PPV}
&\eqdef \Pr(D \mid +)
&& \text{(definition of PPV)} \\
&= \frac{\Pr(+ \mid D) \cd \Pr(D)}{\Pr(+)}
&& \text{(Bayes' theorem)} \\
&= \frac{\text{sens} \cd \Pr(D)}{\Pr(+)}
&& \text{(definition of sensitivity)} \\
&= \frac{\text{sens} \cd \text{prev}}{\Pr(+)}
&& \text{(definition of prevalence)} \\
&= \frac{\text{sens} \cd \text{prev}}{\text{sens} \cd \text{prev} + \paren{1 - \text{spec}} \cd \paren{1 - \text{prev}}}
&& \text{(probability of a positive test)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-ppv-bayes-exr}

:::
